sub_graphs.title: EIP-2700: Event Listener Registration
sub_graphs.description: Models the state transitions when registering event listeners with an Ethereum provider

nodes.label: No Listeners Registered
nodes.description: Provider has no registered listeners for a specific event name

nodes.label: Call on() Method
nodes.description: Client invokes provider.on(eventName, listener) to register a callback

nodes.label: Listener Registered
nodes.description: Provider has registered the listener for the specified event

nodes.label: Call on() with Same Listener
nodes.description: Client registers the same listener function again for the same event

nodes.label: Duplicate Listener State
nodes.description: Implementation-dependent: may callback once or once per registration

edges.label: MAY callback once or multiple times

external_entities.name: Client Application
external_entities.description: DApp or web application registering event listeners with the provider

sub_graphs.title: EIP-2700: Event Emission and Callback
sub_graphs.description: Models how registered listeners receive callbacks when events occur

nodes.label: Listeners Active for Event
nodes.description: One or more listeners registered for a specific event name

nodes.label: Named Event Occurs
nodes.description: The blockchain/provider detects a named event has occurred

nodes.label: Invoke Registered Listeners
nodes.description: Provider MUST call each registered listener with event parameters

nodes.label: Listener Callback Executed
nodes.description: The listener function has been called with event data

sub_graphs.title: EIP-2700: Event Listener Removal
sub_graphs.description: Models the removal of event listeners using removeListener

nodes.label: Listener Currently Registered
nodes.description: A listener is registered for a specific event and will receive callbacks

nodes.label: Decrease Callback Count
nodes.description: Provider MUST decrease the number of times it calls listener per event by one

nodes.label: Callback Count Reduced
nodes.description: Listener will be called fewer times per event (or not at all if count reaches zero)

external_entities.name: Client Application
external_entities.description: DApp removing previously registered event listeners

sub_graphs.title: EIP-2700: Provider Trust Boundary
sub_graphs.description: Models the trust relationship between client applications and the injected provider

nodes.label: Provider Injected into Page
nodes.description: An Ethereum provider object has been injected into the page context

nodes.label: Implicit Trust Established
nodes.description: User implicitly trusts the provider or has explicitly connected

nodes.label: Client Interacts with Provider
nodes.description: Client application calls provider methods assuming trustworthiness

nodes.label: Provider Controls Event Data
nodes.description: Provider has full control over what event data is passed to listeners

external_entities.name: Wallet Extension
external_entities.description: Browser extension or application that injects the Ethereum provider

ambiguities.text: Provider 'MAY choose to either callback the listener one time or one time per call to on' for duplicate listeners
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume implementation-specific behavior. Applications should not rely on specific duplicate listener behavior and should avoid registering duplicates.

ambiguities.text: No specification for what happens when removeListener is called with a non-existent listener
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume it should be a no-op with no error thrown, similar to standard event emitter behavior.

ambiguities.text: Specific event names and their payloads are intentionally excluded from this specification
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume event names and payloads are defined by separate EIPs (e.g., EIP-1193 for 'connect', 'disconnect', 'chainChanged', 'accountsChanged').

implicit_assumptions.description: Users implicitly trust the injected provider to behave correctly and not emit false events
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Malicious providers could emit fake events (e.g., fake 'accountsChanged') to trick applications into incorrect behavior

implicit_assumptions.description: The provider object is injected by a legitimate wallet extension, not a malicious script
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Man-in-the-middle attacks possible where a malicious script intercepts provider calls or injects a fake provider

implicit_assumptions.description: Client applications properly clean up listeners when no longer needed
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Memory leaks and unexpected behavior if orphaned listeners continue receiving callbacks
